Loading the model
Drag to turn. Scroll or pinch to zoom. Right-drag to move.

The motion is drawn from the CAD's own numbers and shows the intended gait. It is not a test result. 106,520 triangles.

Five changes for water

  • One dry vessel. Both motors, the lead screw and every wire sit in one vessel in the tail. Its joints are flat gaskets on six tie rods. Rev 2: the auger's lip seal runs on a hardened, ground dowel pin, the pushrod seals with two U-cups, and the cables pass through bought WetLink penetrators.

  • Spoil leaves as slurry. The auger feeds a chamber behind the thrust spider. One hose takes slurry out. A second brings dilution water in.

  • Setae shoes. Rev 2: curved shoes that hug the body, on M2's own clevises and pins. Going forward they fold to 4°. Slipping back, they open to 35° and bear on the mud.

  • The telescope runs wet. Its key slot is capped and a rubber ring wipes the spigot.

  • The astroworm's crown. Gauge rim with teeth, a 45° scroll cone to the throat, three twisted blades with block pick holders and nine staggered picks, and a fluted pilot bit.

Checked by script

  • 149 interference runs clear, at both stroke ends, shoes open and shut. 29 controls all register.
  • 26 of 26 parts measured inside 130 × 130 × 125 mm.
  • Leak model: 21 cases pass. Taking out any one of the 8 seals is found.

Not tested

  • Nothing has been printed, assembled or put in water.
  • No outside review yet.
  • Anchor hold is an estimate: the shoes about 1.24 times what the dig stroke needs.
